title: perf-bench-scratch-ryan-kim-2026-03-31
content:
Title: KV-cache + batching microbench (scratch)
Owner: Ryan Kim (eng-serving-runtime)
Collaborators: Maya Lopez, Sam Park
Date: 2026-03-29 to 2026-03-31
Status: draft / notes-to-self

Objective:
- Quick iterative runs to quantify p50/p95 latency and sustained throughput (tokens/s) for the Llama2-13B-CHAT-ish variant on A10G nodes.
- Compare KV-cache enabled vs disabled, and small vs large batching policies. Check impact on tail latency.

Env / baseline:
- Model: llama2-13b-chat-2048 (float16, fp16 runtime path)
- Hardware: single A10G (48GB) test node; Docker image: rw-infer:v1.6.2-dev
- Sequence length: prompt 128 tokens, gen 512 tokens => total 640 tokens path (we measure per-request end->end generation)
- Client: locust-style harness that issues REST calls to local dedicated endpoint (no network variance)
- Metric collection: Prometheus + Grafana; also local harness logs p50/p95 and tokens/s per second stamp
- Warmup: 200 requests to populate any caches and JIT paths

Commands (harness snippets):
- ./run_harness --endpoint http://10.0.2.5:8080/v1/generate --model llama2-13b-chat --batch-size 1 --requests 1000 --prompt-file sample_prompts.txt
- toggles: --kv-cache on|off  ;  --batch-granularity small|large

Experiment matrix (quick):
- A: kv-cache=off, batching=small (batch size ~1-4)
- B: kv-cache=off, batching=large (batch size ~16-32)
- C: kv-cache=on,  batching=small
- D: kv-cache=on,  batching=large
- E: kv-cache=on,  batching=large, prefix-caching-enabled (reuse across similar prompts)

Raw results (median of 3 runs each, each run = 1000 steady-state requests after warmup):
- A (no-cache, small): p50=420ms, p95=980ms, tokens/s=680
- B (no-cache, large): p50=360ms, p95=1150ms, tokens/s=2200
- C (cache, small): p50=210ms, p95=480ms, tokens/s=1250
- D (cache, large): p50=190ms, p95=560ms, tokens/s=3600
- E (cache+prefix): p50=130ms, p95=320ms, tokens/s=4200

Observations / quick analysis:
- KV-cache gives ~2x improvement in p50 and ~1.8-2x on tokens/s for small batching. Good for latency-sensitive flows.
- Large batching pushes tokens/s massively (D/E) but increases tail (p95) in some configs (see B p95 1150ms -> higher than A p95). This is because with large batching we occasionally see queuing when request arrival is bursty in the harness.
- Prefix-level caching (E) is the most efficient: it both lowers latency and increases throughput by reducing repeated attention computation. This assumes a meaningful prefix reuse pattern.
- p95 behavior: cache+large batching (D) sometimes shows tail spikes (job scheduling interference). Need to correlate with node-level CPU/GPU metrics.

Simple ascii chart (tokens/s):
- A: |||||||| 680
- B: |||||||||||||||||| 2200
- C: |||||||||||||| 1250
- D: |||||||||||||||||||||||||| 3600
- E: |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| 4200

Notes on variance:
- Each data point is median of 3 runs; run-to-run variance for p95 can be +/- 8-12% depending on background system noise.
- Observed occasional GPU memory fragmentation warnings in container logs during long runs (>30m). Follow-up: rotate container between runs.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Re-run with sequence length = 1024 gen to see gen-length scaling (512 -> 1024). Expect roughly linear drop in tokens/s for pure generation portion.
- Add per-request KV-hit-rate logging to quantify % of cache hits for prefix experiments.
- Try quantized model path (int8) on same node image to compare throughput vs latency tradeoffs. (PR #789 has initial quantization support)
- Correlate p95 spikes with host metrics (nvtop, dmesg, OOM logs).
- Run multi-node test (2x A10G behind routing policy) to see autoscale behavior and per-request routing latency overhead.

Questions / open:
- How stable is prefix caching at production scale when prompts are noisy? Need to build a synthetic workload representing product traffic (mix of short/long prompts, user session reuse).
- Should we make cache TTL per-customer or global? (privacy + memory tradeoffs).

Raw logs: (local harness snippets)
- [2026-03-30T14:03:21Z] RUN START A (no-cache, small)
- [2026-03-30T14:15:02Z] RUN DONE A: p50=422ms p95=978ms tokens/s=672
- [2026-03-30T15:00:10Z] RUN START C (cache, small)
- [2026-03-30T15:12:05Z] RUN DONE C: p50=208ms p95=472ms tokens/s=1264

Notes-to-self for write-up: include Grafana panels for GPU utilization, kernel launch metrics; annotate runs where host CPU spiked (suspect background cron job on node). Reach out to infra to pin test nodes or use dedicated CI pool.

Bottom line (scratch): KV-cache + moderate batching seems best for mixed latency/throughput requirements. For strictly max throughput use large batching + prefix reuse, but need to manage tail latency via queueing policies or separate low-latency tier.

-- Ryan
